notes.title: Patch 2.8
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker!
This update focuses on major bug fixes and stability improvements across environments, combat, and UI systems. Thank you for your reports and feedback!

🛠️ Major Fixes & Gameplay Stability

 Anomalies Getting Reset when Fusing Characters
Fixed a major issue where activated anomalies would reset after fusing characters or reaching the Amalgam. Anomalies now persist correctly through fusion and transitions.

Getting Stuck in Level Geometry (Forge)
Patched multiple wall holes in the Forge where players could wall jump out of bounds or into unintended areas. 

UI & Gameplay Stability
Addressed a rare crash triggered when hiding specific UI elements. Menus and popups should now close safely without freezing or crashing the game. 

🤖 Enemy & Environment

 Enemy & AI Behavior
Improved AI stability around turn tiles and unusual surfaces. Enemies should behave more predictably and no longer cause errors when pathing through tight corners.

Enemy Pathfinding
Fixed a rare issue where enemies could become stuck or confused, especially near edges or obstacles. Their movement logic is now sharper and more reliable.

Enemy Rewards
Resolved a bug where enemy defeats could break reward logic or cause gameplay hangups. Rewards now drop and resolve as expected. 

🎥 Camera & Environmental Fixes

 Camera & Level Navigation
Fixed an issue where the camera could lose track of players or enemies, especially when entering/exiting specific zones. Transitions are now smoother and more consistent.

Water & Environmental Hazards
Addressed a bug where exiting water could cause gameplay systems to break. Swimming and jumping out of water should now function correctly and without side effects.

Pitfalls & Respawning
Fixed a crash that could occur when characters (player or enemy) fell into pits and later respawned. Fall and recover mechanics now behave as intended.

Defense Grid Projectiles
Fixed a crash caused by projectiles sticking to enemies or overlapping with other projectiles in defense grid setups. Laser traps are now deadlier and safer (for your hardware). 

🩸 Health & UI

 Health UI Glitches
Squashed a rare bug that broke health bar updates during scene transitions or menu activity. Health indicators now update consistently and without errors. 

Thanks for playing and keep the feedback coming!
Have fun, and we'll see you out there in the multiverse!

notes.title: Anomaly Warp Update Out Now
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.
Trinity Fusion's third major free content update is now live!

Introducing Anomaly Warp, which lets you customize your run with extra challenges, which sometimes compel you to switch up your gameplay strategies.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/d63f4679154db19c3483451db55a194f804011cb.png


Bossless Rush
All main boss encounters are removed from the run, focusing on a more streamlined experience

Dimensional Shuffle
Enemies from various branches of the multiverse can spawn in any stage, creating unpredictable encounters outside of their usual zones

Escalating Threat
Enemies will get stronger, move faster and have more Health the longer you stay on the same level.

Desync
Maya's psychic link to her counterselves can be disrupted by enemy attacks.
If the link's integrity hits zero, you will be sent back to the Citadel.
Strengthen the link by defeating enemies.

Fortified Foes
Heavy or elite enemies enter combat protected by a shield that must be broken before damaging their main health

Psychic Austerity
Disable all health and regen related psychic augments

Accelerated Hostility
All medium or large enemies move and attack faster if you take too long to clear a room, punishing slow play.

Heavy Taxes
Shop prices increase after every single purchase, making resources scarcer and strategic shopping more crucial.

Enraging Strikes
Whenever you hit an enemy, it briefly gains a damage buff for a few seconds. (stacking)



The Anomalies can be turned on in the Citadel, at the same portal you start your run.
To unlock them, you’d first need to activate any one of the world harmonizers (beat Extant Decay, Steward One or the Ewer Eminence).

Even if you don’t complete the run, you’ll still earn bonus Orbs and Chips for braving these heightened perils.

This patch also brings various minor bug fixes, removes the direct portal to the Citadel Labs and brings some economy balancing changes, especially to the coin drops, which tended to grow way too much, especially if playing the Endless Mode.


We look forward to seeing your death/success screens, with the Anomaly Threshold filled up as much as possible!
If you have any feedback, let us know on our Discord! We're there every day to listen and chat with the players.

Have fun, and we'll see you out there in the multiverse!

notes.title: Free DLC #2: Sundered Spaces, Is now available!
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.
Trinity Fusion's second free content update is now live!

Our second free expansion to Trinity Fusion is now live on Steam, including a new Biome, a new enemy type and a much-requested World Map to help people navigate our now slightly-bigger multiverse!

[previewyoutube=ewdju2C-0-4;full][/previewyoutube]
Now, let's get into what's new:


New Biome: Resonance Halls

The Ewer’s first attempt to enter the In-Between ended in disaster, costing them one of their Greater Minds and opening breaches between the three worlds outside of Prime. Their second attempt to create a tunnel between worlds is currently underway, in a place they call the Resonance Halls.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/a6f305a94030c8ee07a332de37f461a72ee8af5a.jpg
The Resonance Halls are built around the Grapple and Wave Bash abilities, providing the player with several opportunities to fling themselves up vertical corridors and over pits. Players will need to be on their toes, as they’ll need to adapt quickly to the enemies waiting for them when they land.


A Multiversal World Map

Having trouble reaching a specific location in the multiverse? The new World Map can help you plan out your runs! Selecting a location that you’ve previously visited on the map will show you where each of the level’s exits will lead.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/0ea11848b43f28560888061df6c396d041edfe01.jpg
You can find the world map by zooming out all the way on the local area map.


Other small things:


 Attack ranges for the Judge and Preeminence have been modified
 The HP for the non-Elite versions of the Judge and Preeminence has been significantly reduced to put them more in-line with normal enemy units.
 Cooldown Quake can no longer fire several times in quick succession and wipe out everything on-screen
 Wrist Claws Attack Speed increased by ~30%
 Minor localization updates and other minor bugfixes

Wrapping up

And that's it for the Sundered Spaces update! We hope you enjoy flinging yourself through the new level. If you have any feedback, let us know on our Discord! We're there every day to listen and chat with the players.

Have fun, and we'll see you out there in the multiverse!

notes.title: Free DLC #1: Mutagenesis, is now available!
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.

Introducing the first FREE DLC for Trinity Fusion: Mutagenesis.

This is just the first of multiple free expansions that we will be adding to Trinity Fusion over the coming months. So, without further ado, the trailer:

[previewyoutube=PbsDrciUeV0;full][/previewyoutube]
New Location: The Hive

Hidden away deep in the bowels of the Underworld is The Hive, a new biome that expands the number of Underworld locations from 3 to 4.

Down here, a disgusting, fleshy substance has grown over the walls and floors; almost as if a set of living guts are taking shape along the walls of the caverns. The level is filled with large chambers lined with pools of acid, connected by claustrophobic corridors with little room to maneuver.

It’s a longer and more challenging level than any of the others within the Underworld, with harsher fights and some optional tricky platforming areas.

New Enemies

Speaking of harsher fights, the Mutagenesis DLC comes with a handful of dangerous new enemies. Not only will you encounter new Elite versions of older enemies with their own new twists, two entirely new enemies are being added as well.

The Judge
You might remember them from the story! The judge tries to keep their distance, teleporting away from the player and firing small projectiles that spread out into a wall of small projectiles over time.

The Preeminence
Another nasty projectile user with a teleport, except this one will teleport TO you, chasing the player down once they have eyes on Maya.

The Preeminence will not only appear in the Hive, but will also show up as a rare enemy in the Ewer City.

Wrapping up

There are a handful of smaller changes under the hood, but this update is mostly about that SWEET NEW CONTENT.

We have even more levels, enemies and secrets still in the works. Let us know what you think of the Mutagenesis update on our socials and our Discord, and we'll see you out there in the multiverse!

notes.title: Trinity Fusion is now Verified on Steam Deck!
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/b34fc4cb9f23c1c711121e8033c38932280d967e.png

We know just how well roguelikes work on mobile platforms. Being able to start, pause or resume up a run whenever and wherever you get the itch to go again just fits the genre perfectly. When the Deck was announced, we knew that we had to make sure those players were treated like first-class citizens.

Now, all that effort has paid off, and Trinity Fusion is fully Verified on the Steam Deck!

We've added a few tweaks to the game over the last two weeks to make the experience even better. Players can now combine different input methods and controllers, using both simultaneously. You can seamlessly go from playing on the Deck's built-in controls, dock it to your TV and grab your controller (or keyboard) of choice without any fiddling with controller assignments.

We hope you all enjoy the recent updates, and we'll see you out there in the Multiverse!

notes.title: Update 1.1 - Parries and more
notes.content:
Hello, hitchhiker.

It's been just over a month since Trinity Fusion's 1.0 release on Steam, and we're back at work after the holiday break plugging away at new content, as well as working through your feedback and bug reports.

Today's update is the first in a series of updates we'll be making while we work on the game's first proper content expansion. But we'll get to that later. For now, PARRIES.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/f23d3208f335e3ec53a4f18b9951d7fc74b501f6.gif

A common request throughout the game's development was to add some defensive abilities. So, since we're not a fan of the player running around with a shield, we're adding a Parry system to the game, allowing players to deflect or reflect incoming attacks, provided that their timing is on-point.

The full patch notes

Parry System
The Parry is now available as an equippable Psychic Augment. A skill-based defensive option, parries can reflect projectiles back at the enemy that casted them and send melee enemies reeling, instantly putting them into a stun state.

When equipped, just tap the 'Interact' button the moment before an attack hits you to parry it. Successful parries can be instantly canceled out of, including into more parries! Try it out on rapid projectile attacks like Steward One's metal plates. Just don't miss the timng :)

Spectral Scanner
Another new Augment, the Spectral Scanner can be used to scan for and highlight nearby secret areas at a small energy cost.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/96e294e10ce711b61aa313b684783dfdad5ed66e.gif

Bug Fixes:

 The achievement “Amplifier Overload” now correctly unlocks after equipping 5 powerups, matching the description. Previously it required 6.
 It’s no longer possible to get save files softlocked by quitting the game during the “confrontation” cutscene.

Amps

 Stun Spreader - Now stuns enemies instead of staggers them.
 Guard Breaker - Now inflicts guaranteed crits on stunned enemies.

Wrapping up
That's the 1.1 update! Thank you so much for playing our game and all the positive feedback you've been sending our way. As always, let us know what you think of the update on the Steam Forums and on our Discord.

Have fun, and we'll see you out there in the multiverse!

notes.title: Year-end patch notes!
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.

We're back from our holiday break and are hard at work on updates! We hope you enjoyed the Santa hats everyone was wearing in the Citadel, but we've been told that it's probably best to put the decorations away sooner rather than later.

Anyway, on to the patch notes!

Major Bugfixes

 Fixed the unlock conditions for Endless Mode. To access it, players will need to defeat the final boss on Veteran or Hardcore difficulty.
 Fixed a bug where players could get softlocked and unable to attack after equipping a large number of weapons and items, usually during longer runs.
 Fixed issues with collapsing platforms in the in-between that allowed players to phase through certain walls.

Minor Bugfixes

 Fixed a bug which could cause Relan to never return to his station on the top floor of the Citadel
 Fixed a similar issue causing a clone of Issac to randomly hang around the Recall Pods.
 Fixed an issue where Claw 17 could not be rescued due to the Director being unavailable.

Amps and Synergies

 Critical Vampire now has a cooldown of 20 seconds after activating.
 The “Rich Get Richer” synergy has been modified to cap out at a 30% bonus to coins earned. It was previously uncapped which led to ludicrous gains in Endless Mode.
 Adjusted the UI when talking to Nalimyet to only display Amps and Synergies currently in the game. More are coming, but we get how that was confusing.

Other gameplay stuff

 Endless Mode has seen a handful of tweaks to the enemy scaling. Longer runs should now feel much more challenging than they did before.
 Improved the traversability of the Amalgam to prevent players from getting stuck.
 Improved the traversability of the Fortress to prevent players from getting stuck.
 Changed the "hidden map" curse to only hide the minimap. The pause screen map is now unaffected.

And that's it for this one! We hope you're enjoying the game. If you are, please leave us a review! It helps out more than you might think.

Have fun, and we'll see you out there in the Multiverse.

notes.title: First Post-launch patches!
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.

We hope you've been enjoying the 1.0 release of Trinity Fusion! We actually got so swept up in the excitement and watching all the streams, we actually forgot to make an announcement that the game was out. Whoops!

Anyway, we want to thank you all for playing the game, for the reviews, the bug reports and suggestions. It helps out a lot more than you might realize.

Speaking of bug reports and suggestions, you might have noticed that we've been pushing updates pretty much every other day since launch, and we're overdue for a Patch Notes post. So:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/9c43370166c2b01922e88117dbd4f892099460b6.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/33f9e57a9f3223504b7c2f02be2bed3990f690ce.png

New Features

 Added support for 21:9 and 16:10 aspect ratios


 No more black bars on Steam Deck!
 Our levels and intro / outros weren’t exactly designed with ultrawide resolutions in mind, so if you find any graphical oddities near the edges of levels, please let us know about them so we can clean those up!

 Added a screen detailing some upcoming content plans and a message from the dev team for returning players.
Bug fixes
 Fixed a rare crash when loading a save file.
 Fixed a bug preventing the "No Gods or Masters" achievement from being earned.


 If you have beaten the Ewer Eminence previously and did not get the achievement, you will need to defeat them again to earn the achievement

 Fixed a bug in City Walls allowing players to get stuck out of bounds or fall through the level.
 Fixed several issues that could prevent progress or cause the player to lose a permanent traversal ability
 Fixed a few issues that were causing softlocks for some players. (things like suddenly not being able to attack or jump should be fixed)
Levels and progression:
 Fixed an issue that prevented players from navigating through the Amalgam if they had not collected either the Wave Bash or Grapple Arm.
 Updated some of the graphics in City Walls.
Enemy updates
 Tweaks to the Extant Decay and [REDACTED]’s attack patterns to be a little less frustrating.
 Wasps can no longer be pushed through walls.
Once again, thank you so much for playing our game. We have more content in the works that we'll be releasing next year, but for now we hope you enjoy these smaller updates.

Have fun, and we'll see you out there in the Multiverse.

notes.title: Trinity Fusion 1.0 launches THIS FRIDAY, December 15th!
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.

This is it, the last week of Early Access! Trinity Fusion launches with 1.0 status this Friday.

First, and before anything else, we want to thank all of you for your support and feedback over the last nine months we’ve been in Early Access. Among other things, we don’t think we would have landed on the kind of “special sauce” that we needed like our new upgrade system without your feedback. It’s been awesome developing the game with you all.

So, from all of us at Angry Mob Games:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/6996eafcdda8ef06915249f36ce66b11fa3f63fc.png

Patch Notes:

The Story's final chapters, revealed.
Trinity Fusion's story, crafted with the help of the amazing Ada Hoffmann, is now complete.

Investigate mysterious messages left across the multiverse that urge Maya and her counterselves to return to the In-Between, where major revelations await them.
 Save Claw 17 from the Overworld.
 Access terminals throughout the multiverse to discover details about its origin and history.
 Activate the Harmonizers, explore the unstable fused universes of the Amalgam and fight off one last foe that's [REDACTED] to re-unite the multiverse as one stable whole once again.
Fully voiced, emotional and hiding a couple of big surprises, we're trying really hard to sell it without straight-up spoiling the best parts.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/a782534daa46a156958ccaa8ba566592709a5ec6.png

New location: The Amalgam
The result of an incomplete fusion, the Amalgam remixes locations from across the multiverse and the In-Between into new arenas and platforming challenges. It can be only be reached after activating two or more of the Harmonizers.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/d49d3865a6434e7e24cf3d5e602eb11316599008.png

A huge polish pass over the entire UI
We'll let the screenshots speak for themselves on this one.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/ff0d854c27746b273d0876a506df6be66b688b6d.png

New game mode: Endless Mode
Available after completing the game, Endless Mode is what it says it is, a single run that never ends. It does have one small twist though: enemies are randomly replaced with their counterparts from the other universes.

Fight the Ewer in the underworld, or beasts in the Hyperworld! The possibilities are, well, not quite as endless as Endless Mode itself, but there’s still a lot of them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/b0c7200ff26f651811bb7eb3c5a7dba14b53eb74.png

Become the villain with the unlockable Ewer Skin and In-Between alternate starting location
While currently a preorder bonus for the console versions of the game, players on Steam will be receiving the Ewer Skin and Ewer Run game mode that allows players to start runs from within the In-Between as a free bonus in a future update.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/d817bae8cdfd155dc9c16db5ce59876542d516c7.gif

Other things:

 The Heavy Repeater now has piercing shots as an innate perk.
 Added a consumable item that gives two stacks of Barrier.
 Significant changes to the mid-run economy. Players should now get slightly more Orbs and are now much less likely to have enough coins left over to purchase a small island at the end of each run.

Bugfixes:

 Fixed a softlock when fusing characters Thanks to @Farebearclaw and J_G112 for the save files that helped us track that down.
 Fixed an issue causing the item comparison screen from opening on its own when the "interact" button is bound to the same key as the "back" button in menus reported by MapleHero.
 Most Abilities and consumables can now be used midair and on ladders.
 Fixed several instances where characters would say somebody else’s dialogues.
 Fixed a bug where players could get stuck on the loading screen. Thanks to trapinnewyork for the save files that helped us track this down.
 Fixed an issue that could cause players to fire projectiles directly forward instead of where they were aiming.
 Fixed a stutter when opening the Log screen

Additional Steam Deck Optimizations
We've done significant work on optimizing the game, ensuring a 60FPS lock on the Steam Deck and other portables. We've tweaked the Steam Deck graphics preset, aiming for a solid 60 FPS even when the Steam Deck's power draw is capped at 15W in the system's settings.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/ea9211ef2f5cd6b473e66de93305ff6dc0b63ae3.jpg

Wrapping up this post.

We know we already said "thank you" to everyone who has supported us at the top of this post, but since you've made it all the way down here to the bottom, we want to say it again, and a bit more personally this time.

We started working on Trinity Fusion full-time in 2019. It's been a long four years of development, and a whirlwind nine months in Early Access. It's been a long grind getting Trinity Fusion out, and we've been blown away by the reception that we got in Early Access. We funded and published Trinity Fusion ourselves, something we legitimately could not do without you.

The 1.0 release won't be the end, of course. There's still so much more we want to do with this world we've put together. For now though, this is Trinity Fusion. This is the game our tiny team set out to make four years ago. A skillful roguelite with cool environments, crazy-looking enemies, great-feeling movement and extra-chunky combat.

We hope you all enjoy it, and we'll see you out there in the Multiverse.

notes.title: Major Update 4: Prime
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.

Welcome to Major Update #4! This will be the last of the Major Updates before the 1.0 release of the game. Speaking of, we have a new trailer for that...

[previewyoutube=L7MgCKPrSSM;full][/previewyoutube]

That's right, Trinity Fusion leaves Early Access on December 15th! Before that though, we have some new stuff that's ready to go for all our current Early Access players.

This update comes with some huge shakeups to player progression, unlocking all three playable characters from the start, and it includes changes that open up new routes through each run, allowing players to jump between universes by traveling though the In-Between.

It also includes several new weapons for Altara, giving her some much cooler weapons to play with compared to what she had before. Let's get to the patch notes:

Localization updates
By very popular demand, we've added a Brazilian Portuguese localization!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/f212f48c17006c66a7646dca113268e97ab73d06.gif

Optimization and graphics tweaks
In anticipation for the upcoming console release, we've made sweeping optimizations as well as changes to the graphics in The Wastes, Underground Lab, Forge and Subterraria. Everything should look and run even better than before. Take a look at Underground Labs:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/783d84b7d17d5ca254dcdfd1635681c61ddb2824.jpg

Progression Tweaks

 All characters are now unlocked upon the player's first visit to the Citadel.
 When leaving the In-Between, you can now select which universe to continue your run in.
 Players no longer have to fuse characters to travel from one universe to another mid-run.
 Hardcore Mode is now locked until the player defeats the Extant Decay, Steward One and the Ewer Eminence.
New Weapons

Blaze Bombs - A new weapon for Altara. Throws a spread of fire projectiles that will immediately set enemies and the ground around them ablaze. Offers great damage over time and does bonus damage on direct hit.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/201a459511ea10defa81a4f3335770a23be36f9e.gif

Defense Grid - A new weapon for Altara. Electric orbs that stick onto surfaces and enemies that create a point-to-point beam of energy between them. Defense Grid orbs stuck to enemies deal additional damage, at the cost of a reduced lifetime.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/0d5b2784aa0923f3bf55587ca85addd601052982.gif

Resonance Star - A new weapon for Altara. A chargeable projectile that ricochets off of walls and between enemies, with a chance to inflict Weak on anything it damages.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/fed9f6d51269eacf3fbdf8f5aab413cdc3a240fe.gif

Heavy Repeater - A new weapon for Naira. A variant of the Repeater that deals significantly more damage per shot at the cost of a significantly reduced ammo capacity. Firing the weapon in the air also provides Naira with a small boost.

Hyper Mode

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/3c20affe0aa99cbe0a37b3f300c7145c3f8dc578.jpg
Available when playing on Survivor difficulty, Hyper Mode increases your base damage resistance increases each time you die, making subsequent runs slightly easier. Hyper Mode can be enabled or disabled at any time from the Gameplay tab in the Settings menu.

Other updates:


 Fixes for the softlocks that have been reported here on the Steam Forums and on our Discord server.
 Altara’s Arc Pulse weapon now leaves electrical traps on the ground wherever they bounce.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/cb031e006c6c62e4d0a9298faffa2781cd7709b6.gif
 Damage over time effects can no longer kill the player, stopping at 1 HP.
 Explosion sounds from multiple sticky bombs should no longer be deafeningly loud when something causes them all to go off at once.
 Weapons now fade out nicely when not in use.

Wrapping up

That's it for Major Update #4. This is our last Major Update before we leave Early Access and launch into 1.0 We want to thank everyone who's supported us so far, and we hope you enjoy the update. Fow now, it's time for us to get back to work and wrap this thing up. We still have to put the finishing touches on the rest of the story and the fused worlds.

As always, you can keep up with the latest news about the game on X, the social platform accessible via twitter.com and on our Discord!

notes.title: Major Update 3: The Underworld
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.

[previewyoutube=p8vg4hFIEJg;full][/previewyoutube]

Trinity Fusion’s Major Update 3 is now live, featuring:

 A new boss in the Underworld: The Extant Decay
 Updated enemy setups in the Underworld levels. 
 Fine-tuned the combat feel based on the feedback we got at Gamescom and PAX.

 Hit feedback when attacking multiple enemies at once has been reworked to make the player character feel more responsive.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/fed9f6d51269eacf3fbdf8f5aab413cdc3a240fe.gif

Other stuff in the update:

Enemy Changes:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/a58b09d563b14ad64b08292773c76e352d35b400.gif

Weapon Tweaks

notes.title: Major Update 2: The Overworld, is now available!
notes.content:
HELLO, HITCHHIKER
Major Update 2: The Overworld, is now live!

[previewyoutube=pswc-qwAHyM;full][/previewyoutube]
This update brings a lot of community requested features and changes, a new location, two new enemies, a new boss fight, brand new mid-run upgrades and more. Let’s get into it.

New Location: Ewer Fortress
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/44aa81498013c3fca42dd1f65c411252b02376f7.gif
A new location in the Hyperworld, the Ewer Fortress is a maze of stone and circuitry, filled with abstract geometry and expansive rooms. Players will frequently have to put their traversal abilities to use in order to get around.

New Boss: Steward One
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/e1f5c333a1543a3ecc49a4652028477845320711.gif
The final boss and supreme authority of the Overworld, Steward One will make sure your run ends with her. With multiple phases and nasty projectile attacks players will have to use traversal abilities to avoid, Steward One stands as the last obstacle between you and the Overworld Harmonizer.

New Enemy: Ewer Quadra
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/067abde91e7fe54dc3752387d641584120d2d0bf.gif
The first of the new enemies arriving in Major Update 2, The Ewer Quadra is an extremely high-threat unit that fills an unoccupied niche in our current spread of enemies.

Capable of attacking the player from anywhere on-screen, the Quadra makes every single encounter they show up in about them, pestering the player at range with fast shurikens that phase through walls. When the player gets close, it will leap backwards out of melee range and throw its arm assemblies like massive boomerangs to try to keep the player at bay.

Once players have the Quadra all alone, they can (literally) disarm it by shooting its arm assemblies while they're in flight. Once disarmed, the Quadra will be totally defenseless, and will be forced to run from the player, offering a little bit of catharsis after being such a nuisance.

New Enemy: Ewer Arrestor
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/f52b21bd07d9f19d4cb1ad6de9f4f4ecf8c9745d.gif
The second new enemy in Major Update 2, the Arrestor is a new unit found in the Ewer City.

Equipped with a short-range explosive attack and a grappling hook, It will appear as a support unit in most encounters, as well as in locations where it might pull inattentive players off of platforms and into pits.

Hub Changes
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/41de19e85fe2018423ca51c354cf640a71155611.gif
Based on community feedback, players no longer have to run from person to person or walk all the way to the portal to start a new run. You can now simply teleport to wherever you want to go with a handy radial menu.

A new vendor, and a whole new set of upgrades
The Citadel has a new vendor to speak with, offering all-new sets of upgrades and perks to assist you mid-run. Things like:

 Unlocking a Weapon Station that appears before boss encounters where you can upgrade your current weapons.
 The ability to recycle unwanted weapons and items for money mid-run.
 Powerful offensive upgrades for the Teleport Drone.
 Find weapons with a guaranteed number of Perks after a certain power level.

Steam Achievements
A frequent request, Major Update 2 comes with 45 Steam Achievements to… well… achieve. Collect them all!

Misc. Changes

 New Amps, Powerups and Psychic Augments
 Grapple point visuals now change slightly when they are in-range of the player and grappleable.
 Forge has seen a bit of a redesign. It’s now a little bigger, and laid out so that players will need to explore more of the level before finding an exit.
 Changes have been made to hitpause and screenshake to make every attack feel more impactful.
 Added slowmo when staggering Elite or Tank units.
 New platforming challenges have been added to the In-Between that are specific to Kera and Naira.
 Spectral Swords: A new ability for Altara that surrounds her with several floating blades that slice enemies she passes through.
 Countless other minor fixes

When the player gets close, it will leap backwards out of melee range and throw its arm assemblies like massive boomerangs to try to keep the player at bay.

notes.title: Major Update 1 is NOW AVAILABLE
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.
Major Update #1 is now available.
It’s been a little while since Trinity Fusion’s launch into Early Access, and we’ve been a quiet since then. That ends now. Major Update #1 has been released. Let’s go over some of what’s included.

New Location: The In-Between
The instability of the multiverse has given shape to a tumultuous place that sits outside of ‘normal’ space and time, intersecting with and connecting what still remains of the various branches of the multiverse. The Engineers don’t know what to make of it. The Ewer call it “The In-Between”.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/9442bd0139f5bce3c2a63317cd4c73c7c11130c4.png

Gameplay-wise, the In-Between is a gauntlet of small arenas and a handful of platforming challenges with rewards for completing each one. At the end of each challenge, you’ll be given a choice of what challenge you’ll face next, with a hint as to how difficult each option is. Greater challenges offer greater rewards, but just may end your run if you don’t have the skill to complete it.

Maya and her counterselves can reach the In-Between through the doors with red spatial tears found in each level.


Reworked core game loop and mid-run progression

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/64feff6ffff16e0ce3fc88f466c5ae2cd1e7b834.png

We received a lot of feedback on our initial implementation of mid-run perks, which we are now calling Amplifiers to avoid confusion with other mechanics. People wanted to collect more of them, with more drastic and obvious effects. We’re approaching these requests in four ways:

 Adding 50 new Amplifiers to the game and removing some of the less interesting ones from the drop pool.
 Removing the limit on the number of Amplifiers that a player can carry at once.
 Removing the limit on the number of Powerups the player can carry at once.
 Changing Powerups so that they are acquired by collecting enough Amplifiers of the same category, giving players something to work towards mid-run and another thing to consider when selecting Amplifiers.

When selecting Amplifiers, you’ll be able to see which Powerups you will be making progress towards on the top of the selection screen. Powerups have drastic, sometimes game-changing effects, such as Glass Cannon’s doubling of incoming and outgoing damage, Vampire’s HP regeneration, or Mirror Dash’s ability to reflect enemy projectiles back at the caster.

New Combat Features

Per community request, several Primary Weapons now have directional attacks while in the air, allowing players to attack targets above and below them. Attacking airborne units below the player will even bounce the player higher into the air!

On the ground, some weapons have all new moves activated by holding the control stick or movement keys in a specific direction during the weapon’s normal combo. The Double Axes for instance can perform a knockback-dealing final blow, or transition into a spin attack that lasts for as long as the player continues to press the attack button.

Thrown weapons have received a rework. Tapping the attack button will perform close-range strikes, while holding the button will throw the weapon.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/298e74fe1c89d32b45ac3e64b8c45d1e8f3714d2.png

To make this all more manageable, weapons now feature a move list on their descriptions, located above the list of perks the weapon possesses.

New and reworked Status Effects

New Status Effect: Shocked
Enemies that are hit with Electric attacks will have a chance to be afflicted with the Shocked debuff, indicated by electrical sparks crackling across enemy bodies.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/4ab65b99c0f128fafe6cffeee0ac389961f2f21f.gif

Shocked enemies will take a small amount of damage and be briefly paralyzed when they attempt to attack, giving players more time to dodge and evade.

Reworked Status Effect: Burning
Before, there wasn’t much to differentiate Acid and Fire damage. Now, Fire damage stacks. When an enemy reaches five stacks, or when they die while burning, they will combust, setting the ground around them on fire and potentially spreading the effect to nearby units.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/5c7168f74dc8dc3f243f4c7464a09f1b5c5fbe60.gif

New Ability: Glitch Dash
A new ability for Naira, the Glitch Dash temporarily replaces Naira’s slide and air dash with a wildly fast, fully invulnerable burst of movement in whatever direction she is facing. The Glitch Dash deals minor damage to any enemies that Naira passes through while it is active.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/7507543b42b6343baf44c4ef49c56bd5ee1d3d1d.gif

New Passive Ability: Ground Smash
A new passive for Altara, the Ground Smash is exactly what it sounds like, allowing Altara and her Fusions to drop out of the sky and deal damage to enemies below. It's activated by pressing down and the jump button simultaneously.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/29fc5722a648eeae2b47df23767aa55993fc8e65.gif

New Difficulty Settings
We want players to be able to tailor the game’s difficulty to their liking, and the first step we are taking in making the game more accessible is the introduction of three new Difficulty settings that players can select or change when making a new save file, after dying, or in the Citadel by talking to Relan.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/b00dc714f327858480282712d4077c8878cdbf89.gif

Casual
Intended for players who are more interested in seeing the game’s eventual story through, rather than a nail-biting challenge.

 Enemies are less aggressive, attacking less often.
 Arena encounters use alternate enemy formations that are slightly easier.
 Players start with a Health Restore already in their inventory.
 Players are healed to full health before the start of a boss encounter.
 Bosses use modified attack patterns that are easier to deal with.
Standard
The “normal” difficulty. Intended to be challenging, but fair. This is the difficulty that we balance the game around.

Hardcore
More than just a higher difficulty option, Hardcore adds all new gameplay mechanics to contend with.

 Arenas spawn more Waves, Minibosses and Elites than normal.
 Enemy units get stronger, move faster and gain more damage resistance the longer you stay in the same level.
 Elites are more plentiful and may be shielded.
 Incoming damage is increased by 25%
 More support units spawn per level
 Maya’s psychic link to her counterselves can be disrupted by enemy attacks. If the link’s integrity hits zero, you will be sent back to the citadel regardless of your remaining HP. Strengthen the link by defeating enemies.

We plan on expanding these options in the future, including adding the ability to enable and disable any of these modifiers individually to tune the game more to your personal tastes.

The wrapup

With the reworked upgrade system, new weapon moves, new location and new status effects, the game's core loop has substantially changed, and we can't wait to hear what you think of the update here on Steam and on our Discord server once you've had some time to get a feel for it.

As always, we’ll do our best to respond directly to your feedback as we start work on Major Update #2. Until then, have fun exploring the Multiverse!

Join our Discord server: https://discord.gg/TrinityFusion
Follow us on Twitter: https://twitter.com/trinitythegame

notes.title: The first Major Update, "The In-Between" is coming next week!
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.
Next week, we’ll be releasing the first of our Major Updates. While we aren’t ready to share everything just yet, we want to take some time to let you all know how your feedback has shaped what’s coming. No hyperbole, it’s going to substantially change the way the game feels to play.

Reworked core gameplay loop and mid-run progression
First, let’s talk about Amplifiers, or Amps for short, those mid-run upgrades you collect from the stations with the glowing blue crystals. We’ve heard your feedback about them, how you felt constrained by the limits on how many you could carry, how it was difficult to find Amps with good synergies. All of that is changing.

We want players who spend the time to explore and collect Amps to feel like their character is an unstoppable force of nature by the end of each level. To that end, players now receive Amps more often per level, and with no limit to how many they can carry.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/64feff6ffff16e0ce3fc88f466c5ae2cd1e7b834.png

Now, collecting enough Amps of a specific category will activate a Powerup, a special Amp with an extremely powerful effect. For example, collect enough Damage-focused Amps and you’ll unlock Multikill Enhancer or Glass Cannon, or collect Defensive Amps to unlock the Vampire Powerup.

This update will also include new Amps that are more powerful and drastic than what came before, often triggering off of status effects that can be inflicted with specific weapons.

Weapon handling has also seen a significant overhaul. Weapons now have expanded movesets that are exclusive to each archetype. End combos with stun-inflicting finishers, high-knockback launchers, or press the button rapidly to spin endlessly in a tornado of blade strikes. Attack in any direction in the air, knocking around and bouncing off of airborne enemies.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/bc225ca1e17646f88ce8e3c7c71fb8c086c7faf8.gif

All of this should work together to give players another layer of decision-making and strategy when making a build, with more specific upgrades that they can work towards mid-run. 

And players will need these upgrades now more than ever, because even though their counterselves will be more powerful than ever before, so will their foes. We've improved the reaction times of many of our enemies, and adjusted their attacks to make them more challenging to fight individually. The multiverse has never been more dangerous.

A new location: The In-Between
The instability of the multiverse has given shape to a tumultuous place that sits outside of ‘normal’ space and time, intersecting with and connecting what still remains of the various branches of the multiverse. The Engineers don’t know what to make of it. The Ewer call it “The In-Between”.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/a92ecccc607a91961cfacd27e4832a951305a57b.png

This location will bring together trials and opponents from all across the multiverse, so be prepared for a challenge.

And more still to be unveiled…
We’ll have more to share, including the full patch notes, next week when Major Update #1 is released on Steam. Keep an eye out for it!

notes.title: Thank you for a successful launch into Early Access!
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.

After four years of development, we finally launched Trinity Fusion one week ago, and we’ve spent the time since launch watching your streams, scouring social media and reading your reviews and feedback. We want to thank everyone who wrote something either on Steam or on our Discord. We’re actually blown away by the response so far. THANK YOU.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/6996eafcdda8ef06915249f36ce66b11fa3f63fc.png

Now, with the launch out of the way, we want to talk about our update plans for the game as we continue development in Early Access. We plan on pushing smaller updates responding to your feedback frequently in-between our major content pushes that we’ve outlined on our roadmap (which you can find here).

We’d like to share our vision for the first of these smaller updates, which we plan to have ready in the coming weeks. We would appreciate your feedback on this list, as well as your suggestions for what you feel would make Trinity Fusion’s gameplay and meta-progression even better.

Mods
We want to make the mods you select a more interesting process. We’re working on tweaks to provide you with more opportunities to find mods that synergize well with each other as you work towards a good mid-run build that fits your playstyle. We’re also planning on expanding on the current 5 mod equip limit to give players more of an opportunity to put together crazy builds.

Difficulty Settings
Some players wanted a bigger challenge, while others found certain areas a bit too hard. Along with the already implemented Hyper Mode, we’re adding a few new difficulty settings to allow players to tune the game more to their liking. Players will be able to change the settings between runs at the Citadel.

On the highest setting, enemies will receive additional tweaks, responding to the player’s presence faster and more aggressively, making them a bit tougher to defeat, even when you’re one-on-one with them.

Lore and progression
Players were asking for more information in the Lore screen. We’re going to do that as well as add an additional screen at Cirre for the completionists among you to check how much of the game is still undiscovered. You’ll be able to read up on all the enemies, mods, weapons and collectables you have found over the course of your runs.

A new Tutorial
We’re currently starting work on a brand new tutorial level to help players get up to speed about what’s different in Trinity Fusion and its more unique mechanics.

Other Stuff
We’re currently preparing our first patch to the game since launch with a handful of tweaks, bugfixes and quality of life changes based on what you’ve been suggesting and reporting to us. We’ve also made sure to shout out users on our Discord that were particularly helpful in the patch notes. Keep it coming!

notes.title: Patch Notes - Next Fest Demo
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/115edc899ec0fde5d4363e508b53359a32a37614.png

Hello, Hitchhiker.
We've been hard at work on the game since Closed Beta #2, and the Next Fest Demo brings a LOT of changes based on your feedback. Here's a short list of everything we've done since the last time you've traveled the multiverse:

WEAPON DROP REWORK
We heard your feedback! Weapons no longer drop from Blue Chests.

 Blue chests now offer you a choice between two different random items.
 Weapons are now dropped by defeated enemy units throughout the levels.

MULTIVERSE HOPPING
The portal devices you've found previously throughout the biomes now have a new function. You can now:

 Bring a character you have previously unlocked into the current biome.
 Travel to a previously unlocked universe with your current character.

NEW MODS AND POWERUPS
There are a whole bunch of new mods and powerups that should enable more interesting builds. Here are just a few of our favorites:

 Mirror Dash: Dashes reflect projectiles back at the caster.
 Adrenaline Rush: Rapidly defeating enemies temporarily increases your movement/attack speed. Continuing to defeat enemies prolongs the effect.
 Seeking Wisp: Rapidly defeating enemies spawns a seeking projectile.
 Variety Striker: Kills with one weapon temporarily power up your other weapon.
 Volatile Strikes: Defeated enemies have a chance to explode, dealing Fire damage to nearby units.
 Vengeance: Taking damage highlights the enemy that injured you. Your next attack on that enemy is a guaranteed crit.
 AND MORE

NEW CONSUMABLES
Red Chests now have a larger list of consumables, such as:

 Adrenaline Shot: Temporarily boosts move and attack speed by 20%. Stacks with other speed enhancements.
 Rally Banner: Deploys an energy field that massively boosts your Crit chance while inside of it.
 Radial Freeze: Instantly inflicts Freeze against all on-screen enemies.
 Projectile Syphon: Converts incoming projectile damage into healing for a short time.
 AND MORE

OTHER NEW MECHANICS

 New aiming controls for Mouse and Keyboard players while playing as Naira.
 Kera now has an airdodge.
 Difficulty rework: enemy distribution starts a bit easier than the previous demo and escalates in difficulty after reaching certain milestones to give players more of a chance to get familiar with the levels.

NEW MUSIC

 Brand new music for Subterraria and Forge.

NEW MODES

 Boss Rush and Flawless Boss Rush are unlocked by completing the main demo

NEW CUTSCENES

 The bosses have all received new cutscenes that we've worked very hard on.

notes.title: Trinity Fusion - Next Fest Livestream #2
notes.content:
Join us for a special Steam Next Fest livestream where we'll be going over the content of the Next Fest demo, answering questions from the livestream chat, and talking about what comes next for Trinity Fusion and Angry Mob Games!

There will be news and reveals throughout the stream. You won't want to miss this!

What is Trinity Fusion?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/115edc899ec0fde5d4363e508b53359a32a37614.png

Trinity Fusion is a sci-fi action roguelite set in a doomed, manmade Multiverse. Psychically connect with your parallel selves, each with their own weapon specializations, unique abilities, challenges and enemy encounters that overrun their worlds. 

Battle your way through hostile environments like underground caves, fortified Machine prisons, and high-tech sky cities that will fuse to become entirely new worlds that shift and change depending on each player's route through the Multiverse. As the worlds combine, so will your parallel selves, altering the gameplay experience as your pool of available weapons and abilities grows throughout each run.

Coordinate with your other selves in a mission to find a stable Fusion for your universes, before they all fall apart entirely.

Our Reveal Trailer
[previewyoutube=iHahivCgKPU;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: The Boss Rush Beta is halfway over!
notes.content:
Hello, Hitchhiker.

We're about halfway through the Boss Rush Beta period, and we felt like giving you all a little mid-beta update on how things are going! As a reminder, we're running a contest with this beta, challenging players to record themselves pulling off a Flawless Boss Rush.

Each player that pulls it off will get to name an upcoming NPC, and one player will win a brand new Steam Deck! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/ea9211ef2f5cd6b473e66de93305ff6dc0b63ae3.jpg

We currently have just four players that have managed to complete the Flawless Boss Rush. Think you can do it? You still have a few days left! Click here to check out our website for the full contest details and to get your beta key!

Meet the Bosses

This post seemed a little short, so we felt it might be time to reveal a little bit about the bosses you've been fighting. Each of the bosses you've seen so far have their own unique roles within Trinity Fusion. Equipped with devastating abilities and movesets, players will have to adapt and act fast to stand a chance against them.

The Lens Guardian
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/bf0a2ce69e9a02310fa9a165d1ce5e00e66ab397.png
From the Underworld, the Lens Guardian: a three-eyed cybernetic mutant left behind by the Ewer and the Machines to prevent Altara from re-activating the Underworld Lens, a device that will allow Maya to break through the barriers between universes and link up with more of her other selves.

Typhon Two
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/c902f7ffd8e1662755c73c0017d7b266f33d55e1.png
In the Overworld, Kera faces Typhon Two, A massive, tanklike Machine posted at the exit to the underground labs Kera uses to lose her Machine pursuers. Armed with missile barrages, lasers, a rear shield and area-denying energy fields, Typhon Two is equipped to fight Kera specifically.

Ewer Eminence
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/ce39fa3884e81c8aed957192eba435cc5555df5e.png
Finally, Naira will take on the Ewer Eminence, the supreme leader of the Hyperworld and the girls' greatest foe yet. Deciding to take on Naira themselves, The Eminence goes on the offensive, wielding advanced nanotechnology that gives them no shortage of elemental attacks and a unique ability to radically transform themselves mid-fight.

notes.title: Closed Beta Playtest #2 has begun!
notes.content:
Hello Hitchhiker. Closed Beta Playtest #2 has begun!

Since the last Beta, we've been going over your feedback, your streams and videos (yes, all of them) and everything you've written online that we can find. We're massively appreciative of your feedback on our Discord server and online.

This beta will run between now and December 13th.

For this playtest, we've made a boatload of optimizations and minor bugfixes, honestly way too many to list off. If you're playing on a mid-range machine or better, you may not notice much of a difference in the way the game runs (it was already pretty good!), but players on lower-spec machines and Steam Deck should have a smoother experience.

Enough about behind-the-scenes stuff though, onto the patchnotes! Items in BOLD are changes as a direct result of user feedback.

------------------------------------------

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/b86ccf8a160ad07e5f63f821dfea377cbd6e3b5e.jpg

 A new boss at the end of Naira’s path.

 Kera’s Energy Weapons are getting buffed. Jabs and Charge Attacks are much stronger than before.
 Armored enemies without a shield no longer completely Block attacks.

 More dialogue! A little extra story this time around.

 The Beetle enemy in The Wastes can now be attacked from behind.

 Ewer City has a new, heavily optimized background.

 There are now video settings and options in the settings menu.

 Guaranteed Primary and Energy weapon chests at the start of the second biomes
 This is a temporary solution for players sometimes having underleveled equipment while we re-evaluate how we handle enemy and weapon scaling
 10% health restores are replaced with 35% restores

 Changed the unlock order in the Psychic Augments menu
 Permanent health upgrades are now in the first set of unlocks
 Some progression:

 Players will start with only Altara unlocked.
 Kera is unlocked by defeating Altara's boss or after 6 deaths.
 Naira is unlocked by defeating Kera's boss or after 12 deaths.

notes.title: Post-EGX news!
notes.content:
We're back in the studio after EGX London! Thanks to everyone who dropped by the booth to play the game for the first time. It was great finally getting it out in public where people could play it. 

We were overwhelmed by all the positive feedback we got from the demo at the show, and we're hard at work going through the feedback we got. Also, we put together a little aftermovie of our booth at the show, which you can check out here:

[previewyoutube=S6wryPW3syg;full][/previewyoutube]

For those of you who attended the show and played the demo, you probably want specifics as to what's we've already changed for the Closed Beta since we got back. Well,


 We're making a few of the mid-level arenas a little less cruel.
 We're improving the distribution of upgrades and health items throughout the levels.
 We're tweaking the boss attack patterns to give players a bit more time to fight back between attacks.
 We've added a room with upgrade chests and health restores before the boss fights.


Speaking of the closed beta, there's still time to sign up here. We'll have more info to share about exact dates for the Closed Beta and what you can expect from it Soon™

notes.title: Trinity Fusion will be at EGX London!
notes.content:
We're going to be at EGX London this week to show off our current progress on Trinity Fusion with a playable demo!

We'll be in the Rezzed Zone on the show floor every day from September 22-25, right next to the entrance. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42971343/5ef875af80c98057f584d118eb54c542726a5df6.png

Trust us, we'll be hard to miss.

The demo consists of:

 All 3 playable characters
 6 biomes
 2 bosses
And it is tough as hell. Think you can beat it? Come by, hang out, try a few runs and give us your feedback! We're excited to finally get the game out in front of people for the first time and can't wait to see you there!
